reason: The cited evidence shows HEA+WC coatings on steel (not Ti-6Al-4V) can achieve high hardness (E2, E3) and that WC addition promotes carbide formation (E1), but none of the passages address cladding on titanium alloys, metallurgical bonding to Ti-6Al-4V, or the specific dual-phase boundary layer mechanism on this substrate. The hardness and wear reduction claims are extrapolated from different substrate systems without direct support.
premises: Laser cladding of HEA+WC on Ti-6Al-4V produces a metallurgically bonded coating
In situ formation of a dual-phase layer with HEA matrix and WC-derived carbides/W-rich phases
Solution strengthening from HEA and dispersion strengthening from carbides act together
This microstructure inhibits abrasive wear and prevents delamination
Surface hardness increases from ~350 HV to >800 HV and wear rate reduces by factor 2-3
